briefs.title: Tax Politics Turn in Cannabis's Favor as Rescheduling and Psychedelics Momentum Build Nationally
briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax just became a genuine campaign issue, with a major-party nominee courting operators on repeal, while nationally the DEA's Schedule III process and Compass Pathways' fast-tracked psilocybin therapy are moving from promise to paperwork. Operators who adapt supply-chain terms and watch the courts have real upside on both fronts this fall.

local.text: Republican gubernatorial nominee John James is actively courting Michigan's cannabis industry with a pledge to gut the 24% wholesale tax, and operators are responding with cash and support as the industry looks for a political off-ramp from its heaviest tax burden yet.

Not every operator is retreating: Rize, which runs three Upper Michigan locations, has kept growing by negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers to split the wholesale tax burden rather than absorb it alone, even as rival chain Higher Love closed five of its nine U.P. stores.

After a brutal January, Michigan's market found its footing — sales climbed back to $255.4 million in March and held steady near $253.5 million through June, evidence that pass-through, not collapse, is defining the tax's real-world impact.

The industry's two-front legal challenge to the wholesale tax is now heading toward trial, with the first lawsuit proceeding toward a September 2026 court date that could determine whether the tax shrinks, disappears, or triggers refunds for operators statewide.

A Sixth Circuit panel wiped out a $31.8 million jury award to Michigan grower Hello Farms, ruling the underlying contract was federally illegal — a reminder that until rescheduling fully lands, interstate cannabis deals still carry outsized legal risk for operators.

national.text: DEA's expedited Schedule III rescheduling hearings wrapped in mid-July, and the agency has already opened a fast-track federal registration pathway letting state-licensed medical operators use their existing state credentials as conclusive proof of authorization — a live opportunity for operators to start cutting 280E exposure now.

Compass Pathways' synthetic psilocybin treatment COMP360 is riding an FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher and rolling NDA review toward a Q4 2026 submission, with commercial launch readiness targeted for the end of the year — the clearest sign yet that a psychedelic medicine could reach patients on an accelerated federal timeline.

Consolidation is paying off for the majors: Vireo Growth posted Q2 GAAP revenue up 335% year-over-year on the back of the Hawthorne, Eaze and Bridgewell acquisitions and is now absorbing FLUENT, C21 and Planet 13, while Trulieve completed a restructuring to list on the NYSE under ticker TRLV.

Red White & Bloom Brands just closed a transaction establishing operations in Germany and the U.K., inheriting a European platform that dispensed or distributed more than twelve tonnes of medical cannabis in the past year — a sign North American operators are still finding fresh growth abroad even as the domestic market matures.

State governments collected $986.8 million in marijuana tax revenue in Q2 2026, up roughly 11% year-over-year and nearly 16% higher than Q1 — solid demand growth, though a companion industry survey found only 5% of cannabis businesses call commercial credit readily available, underscoring why 73% of respondents are banking on rescheduling to change their operations.
